title: The Pauline Epistles
description: An exegetical and theological study of Paul's thirteen letters. Students examine Paul's life and mission, the structure and argument of each letter, and the major themes of Pauline theology: the gospel, justification, union with Christ, the law, the Spirit, the church, ethics and eschatology. Interpretive debates - such as the 'new perspective on Paul', Romans 7 and 9-11, gender roles, and authorship questions - are presented fairly from the major traditions' own sources.

quiz_bank.answer_key: In Christ's death, resurrection and the Spirit's gift the new age has begun - believers are justified, raised with Christ, new creation - yet they still await the redemption of the body, final victory over sin and death, and Christ's return; ethics flow from being what they already are in Christ.

lessons.paper_prompt: Write a 1,500-2,000 word paper arguing for what you consider the center (or integrating theme) of Paul's theology. Engage at least three Pauline letters, interact with at least two library sources representing different traditions (for example Augustine, Luther, Calvin, Wesley, Aquinas; cite as Author, Title, section), and address the strongest objection to your proposal.
